messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a regression on staging where KV cache memory grows steadily on long-context requests and continuous batching ends up blocking at head-of-line. Repro steps and quick traces below.
liam: Can you paste the repro steps?
maya: Steps: 1) run chat replay with 64k context on ded-4g, 2) enable continuous batching (default), 3) feed long tails. Repro ~15m.
liam: repro'd locally, got similar mem growth. Any recent changes to batching heuristics?
sara: rolled batching heuristics PR  #4129 last week — we relaxed split threshold to reduce small-batch overhead. Thought it would help throughput.
maya: That matches timeline. Profiling shows a lot more merge events then. The merge code paths are touching KV allocator more often and we see more fragment churn.
jun: Pprof snippet (top functions):
```
cpu: 2mins
  30%  kvcache.MergeBatches
  18%  kvcache.AllocateFragment
  12%  kvcache.EvictPage
  8%   runtime.mallocgc
  6%   runtime.scanobject
```
liam: So more merges -> more small fragment allocations -> fragmentation + eviction churn. That would explain mem growth and paging.
sara: Hmm. The intent of relaxing split threshold was to avoid head-of-line latency for tiny batches. But the side effect might be too many merge operations for long-context traces where KV pages are large.
maya: Also noticed kernel selector falling back to 16-bit fallback kernels during merge-heavy periods (see logs). So CPU work per token increases as well. Perf-ci flagged a regression: p50 +32%, p95 +55% for long-context chat workload.
perf-ci: Regression alert: job=staging/longctx, metric=latency_p50, delta=+32%, since=1767600000.
liam: Do we have flamegraphs for the head-of-line blocking?
jun: Attached flame link: https://internal/fg/1767777788 — shows long tail where a single batch merge holds kvslot locks and queues up following tail batches.
maya: Observed queue backlog: continuous-batcher #1 merges batch A and then waits on evict path, blocking batch B which has the earlier KV pages, causing head-of-line.
sara: Could be interaction between merge atomicity and eviction sweep. If merge holds a global fragment lock while calling EvictPage, it can cause long stalls.
liam: Quick mitigation idea: make merge non-blocking for eviction path — spawn background evict goroutine or release fragment lock before calling eviction.
jun: Also we could early-bail merges when total fragment footprint exceeds X% of reserve to force split and reduce churn.
maya: Experimented with aggressive split heuristic locally (config snippet):
```
continuous_batch:
  split_threshold_tokens: 1024  # was 4096
  merge_window_ms: 6           # was 12
  max_merge_ops_per_sec: 200   # throttle merges
```
maya: With that config mem growth rate halves and p50 improves ~12%, but overall throughput drops slightly.
sara: Short-term revert of PR #4129? Or gate it behind long-context flag?
liam: We should avoid full revert — try canary config on staging and dedicated pools.
maya: Deployed a quick canary with throttled merges to staging.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: staging/kv-batching-canary by maya.
maya: After canary (30m) — backlog reduced, eviction spikes lower, kernel fallback occurrences down by ~70%.
perf-ci: Canary metrics: latency_p50 -12%, mem_leak_rate -48% on canary hosts.
jun: Root cause hypothesis: relaxing split threshold increased batch merge frequency; merge path is not eviction-safe (holds locks) and interacts poorly with large-page eviction and allocator, causing fragmentation and head-of-line stalls. Also increased CPU due to kernel fallbacks under merge pressure.
sara: Action items: 1) Add unit/integration test for merge+evict race, 2) make merge release heavy locks before eviction, 3) add merge throttling knob and ops/sec limit, 4) tune kernel selector to avoid fallback during merge spikes.
liam: I'll own #1 and #2. maya please run extended canary + perf traces. sara will own #3 and #4.
maya: Will run 6hr canary and attach pprofs.
sara: Filed follow-ups: infra ticket INF-879 (merge lock -> eviction refactor), perf ticket PERF-221 (kernel selector hysteresis), and ops ticket OPS-441 (staging canary + config).
maya: Thanks — keeping this thread as running diary. If anyone sees related alerts ping here. :eyes:
liam: Nice debugging. :clap:
perf-ci: Note: regression alert cleared for canary group.
maya: I'll post pprof + flamegraphs once 6hr run completes.
liam: TY.
